mzcxc6:341: The article reveals a core contradiction: ** The rules in CLAUDE.md are essentially "suggestions", not "constraints" **. This is a fundamental problem faced by almost all AI programming tools—LLM works based on probability; no matter how good the context understanding is, it cannot guarantee that rules are followed every time. The solution of Hooks essentially moves human-machine collaboration from the "prompt layer" down to the "execution layer". The traditional approach (writing CLAUDE.md conventions) relies on the AI "remembering" rules at runtime, and the result depends on randomness; Hooks insert deterministic logic at key lifecycle nodes, turning rules into "processes that will definitely execute" rather than "prompts that might be remembered". The deeper meaning of this shift is: it redefines the boundary of human-machine collaboration. Prompts are responsible for "direction guidance", and Hooks are responsible for "bottom-line enforcement". For operations that require mandatory guarantees (such as file protection, branch restrictions), Hooks provide determinism that prompts cannot provide.
